mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tight labor market, which may lead to wage inflation and subsequently negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST MoM > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO MoM < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances during a monetary tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS MoM < -1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% year-over-year, it signals inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.
